A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same pre-trained model selection study. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including the material added in v4.

before.justification: v3 reports original fine-tuning experiments measuring OOD accuracy and calibration, alongside optimizer, regularization and random-seed analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds adaptive calibration error measurements, TerraIncognita results and evaluations with alternative held-out domains.

M1.justification: The pre-trained model selection, fine-tuning procedures, architectures and optimization methods are retained. ACE is introduced as an evaluation metric, not a new training or inference component.

E1.justification: v4 adds evaluation on TerraIncognita with L38 held out, reported in Appendix D.2. The existing DomainBed, Camelyon17 and ImageNet-variant coverage remains; alternative holdouts within retained datasets are protocol extensions.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same ERM, Best Algorithm and Best Model comparison. Table A.1 retains the model roster, and the existing optimizer, pre-training and CLIP comparisons are unchanged. The added analyses use existing model configurations.

E3.justification: v4 adds ACE with adaptive, equal-count confidence bins and additional held-out-domain evaluations for PACS and OfficeHome. These extend the evaluation protocol; the original first-domain holdout, validation-based selection, hyperparameter grids, batch size of 32 and 5,000 training iterations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D.1 and D.3 add substantive checks of two central sensitivities: whether calibration findings depend on ECE's binning and whether scaling trends depend on the selected test domain. These extend the retained seed, optimizer and weight-decay analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds and the same means and standard deviations in Table C.1. There is no added confidence-interval, significance-testing or repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures D.1-D.4 add results showing nearly matching ECE and ACE, scaling trends on TerraIncognita, and outcomes across alternative held-out domains. They also document exceptions, including ConvNeXt-xlarge underperforming smaller models on OfficeHome Product. Table 1 and all original plots retain their results; these are added findings rather than same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: v4 adds Appendix E's informal Theorem E.1 and an entropy/KL-divergence argument that ECE approaches zero under infinite data matching the true distribution and near-zero cross-entropy loss. v3 contains calibration definitions but no corresponding theorem or proof, making this a new theoretical component.

C1.justification: The principal recommendations favoring larger models, larger pre-training datasets and generic training remain. The contribution bullets add an explicit first-study claim about jointly examining dataset and model size across architectures, and recast calibration as a partial explanation of OOD scaling through invariant feature learning.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly interprets scaling as mitigating domain-specific overconfidence and promoting invariant feature learning. Section 2 adds limitations of fixed-bin ECE, while Appendix D.3 attributes exceptions on OfficeHome Product and PACS Photo to performance saturation. These substantially expand interpretation and qualification beyond v3's parallel accuracy/calibration trends.

D1.justification: Appendix A replaces the anonymous code link with a named GitHub repository and identifies the previously anonymous supercomputer as the ABCI Cluster. Hardware specifications, software versions, training budget and existing implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Nixon et al. (2019), Tran et al. (2022), Kadavath et al. (2022), and Dan and Roth (2021). It qualifies the comparison with earlier calibration work by distinguishing IID from OOD settings and explicitly describes agreement with Minderer et al. in OOD settings.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution bullets and Section 5.2 undergo substantial rewriting around OOD scaling and calibration as an explanatory analysis. Related-work discussion is reordered, confidence-calibration terminology replaces broader uncertainty terminology in key passages, and the conclusion and author information are revised.

P2.justification: v4 adopts journal typography, headers and page geometry, relocates Table 1 to the first page and Figure 1 to the second, and adds Figures D.1-D.4. Existing appendix plots are retained as Figures D.5-D.18, with extensive resizing and redistribution through the new layout.

improvement.justification: The ACE and alternative-domain checks strengthen validation of the existing conclusions, while TerraIncognita and clearer resource information provide useful additional support. The overall gain is limited: the core results remain unchanged, and the stronger invariant-feature explanation remains inferential. Appendix E's idealized theorem does not establish that mechanism for finite-data OOD generalization.
